segments.narration: Two girls fooled the creator of Sherlock Holmes. Cottingley, Yorkshire, nineteen seventeen, with a borrowed camera.
Elsie was sixteen and worked at a photographer's. Frances was nine and had told her mother she played with fairies by the beck.
Arthur Conan Doyle got hold of the prints. He was a spiritualist, he was convinced, and he published them in The Strand.
Experts of the day argued about the negatives for years. Nobody thought to ask a sixteen-year-old how she did it.
In nineteen eighty-three both women admitted it: paper cutouts propped on hatpins. Frances insisted to the end that one photo was real.
